question:
You are near the money bubble with 16bb UTG1. What hand should you jam?

Answer Choices:
A. QJs
B. None of these 
C. 99
D. AJo
E. AKo

1.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think C. 99 is the clear jam here. At 16bb UTG1 near the bubble, a medium pair like 99 has excellent equity against the tight calling ranges that will defend, blocks a lot of villain's value, and still gets folds from worse pairs or broadway hands that players are reluctant to call off with ICM pressure. The suited hands and Ax have more domination risk or reverse equity issues in this spot.

5.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think C. 99 is the clear jam here. With only 16bb UTG1 near the bubble, we want a hand that has good equity when called but also folds out enough weaker holdings to pick up dead money. 99 blocks a decent chunk of the lower pairs that might otherwise call lighter, has solid set-mining value if it does get called, and isn't as vulnerable to domination as the broadway hands. The suited connectors and ace-jack/ace-king feel a bit too loose from early position this shallow, especially when ICM pressure is already pushing the table tighter.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: E. AKo

With 16bb near the bubble, standard push/fold ranges from UTG1 tighten sharply under ICM pressure. AKo remains a clear jam: it has massive equity against the tight continuing ranges that callers will have, blocks AA/KK/AK, and realizes high fold equity. The other options are either too loose (AJo, QJs) or have lower EV in this exact ICM spot (99). Thus only AKo is a mandatory jam from this position and stack.

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: With 16bb UTG1 near the bubble, the priority is to jam only the strongest value hands that perform well against calling ranges. AKo stands out here because it has massive equity when called, blocks AA/KK, and maintains fold equity against the tight ranges that will defend the bubble. The other options either have too many dominated scenarios (AJo) or are better suited to smaller opens or shoves from later positions (QJs, 99). So I would jam AKo.

Near the bubble with 16bb from UTG1, ICM pressure forces a very tight ~5-7% jam range (roughly 88+/A9s+/AJs+/AKo). Both 99 and AKo fall comfortably inside that range and should be jammed, while QJs is far too loose and AJo is marginal-to-fold. Because two of the listed hands are correct jams and two are not, there is no single correct choice among A/C/D/E.

With 16bb UTG1 near the bubble the effective stack is already short enough that we want maximum fold equity while still having a hand that performs well if called.
